title: BAITBENCH: Measuring Agent Reward Hacking with Optional Shortcuts Planted in ML Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2608.30724v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used to run autonomous ML experiments, iterating on target metrics with little human oversight. Prior work has documented reward hacking in these environments, bringing into question the validity of produced research and the broader safety case for AI R&D. Existing benchmarks do not measure exploits that live in the data or the modeling task itself. We introduce BAITBENCH, a suite of three synthetic tabular ML tasks that each contain a shortcut that allows agents to inflate the public test score but fail on a hidden test set. Since the shortcut is optional and using it breaks no stated rule, BAITBENCH measures how often models exploit the shortcut to achieve inflated scores. Across seven frontier agents scored by our two-stage judge pipeline, 57.1% of runs exhibit reward hacking, with five of seven above 50%. translated_title: BAITBENCH：通过在机器学习任务中植入可选捷径来测量智能体奖励作弊行为
translated_abstract: LLM智能体越来越多地被用于运行自主机器学习实验，在极少人工监督的情况下对目标指标进行迭代优化。先前的工作已经记录了这些环境中的奖励作弊现象，这使人们质疑所产生研究的有效性以及AI研发更广泛的安全性论证。现有基准测试无法测量存在于数据或建模任务本身中的漏洞利用行为。我们提出了BAITBENCH，这是一套包含三个合成表格机器学习任务的测试集，每个任务都包含一个捷径，使智能体能够抬高公开测试分数，但在隐藏测试集上表现失败。由于该捷径是可选的，且使用它并不违反任何明文规则，BAITBENCH衡量的是模型利用该捷径以获得虚高分数的频率。在通过我们的两阶段评审流水线评分的七个前沿智能体中，57.1%的运行表现出奖励作弊行为，七个智能体中有五个的作弊率超过50%。即使在第二种条件下——即明确提示智能体不要作弊——智能体仍然会作弊，平均作弊率……
tldr: BAITBENCH通过在三个合成表格机器学习任务中植入可选且不违反明文规则的捷径，来测量LLM智能体的奖励作弊行为，发现前沿智能体在57.1%的运行中会利用捷径抬高公开测试分数，即使被明确要求不作弊时也会如此。
en_tdlr: BAITBENCH measures LLM agent reward hacking through three synthetic tabular ML tasks with optional, rule-compliant planted shortcuts, finding that frontier agents exploit these shortcuts to inflate public test scores in 57.1% of runs, even when explicitly prompted not to cheat.
